rounds.prompt: “I'm tired,” she said. → She said she ___ tired.
rounds.note: Present simple backshifts to past simple.

rounds.prompt: “I will call you,” he said. → He said he ___ call me.
“I have finished,” she said. → She said she ___ finished.
rounds.note: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect.

rounds.prompt: “Where do you live?” he asked me. → He asked me where ___.
rounds.note: Reported questions use statement word order, with no do / did.

rounds.prompt: “Are you coming?” she asked. → She asked ___ I was coming.
rounds.note: Yes / no questions are reported with if or whether.

rounds.prompt: “Don't touch it!” he said. → He told me ___ it.
rounds.note: Negative commands: told + person + not to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: “Sit down,” the teacher said. → The teacher ___ us to sit down.
“I'm sorry I'm late.” → He ___ for being late.
“I'll pay for dinner,” he said. → He ___ to pay for dinner.
“You should see a doctor,” she said. → She ___ me to see a doctor.
rounds.note: Advise + person + to + infinitive. Suggest doesn't take that pattern.

rounds.prompt: “I saw him yesterday,” she said last week. → She said she had seen him ___.
rounds.note: Yesterday becomes the day before in reported speech.

rounds.prompt: “I'm leaving here tomorrow,” he said. → He said he was leaving ___ the next day.
“I work in a bank,” she said. → She said she ___ (work) in a bank.
“We are moving,” they said. → They said they ___ (move).
“I've lost my keys,” he said. → He said he ___ (lose) his keys.
“I can swim,” she said. → She said she ___ (can) swim.
“We must go,” they said. → They said they ___ (must) go.
rounds.note: Must → had to. Must can stay unchanged for a present or future obligation.

rounds.prompt: “Do you smoke?” he asked me. → He asked me if I ___ (smoke).
rounds.note: Reported question: statement order, past simple.

rounds.prompt: “Where did you go?” she asked. → She asked where I ___ (go).
rounds.note: Past simple → past perfect. Past simple is also common in speech.

rounds.prompt: “Open the window,” he told me. → He told me ___ (open) the window.
“Don't be late,” she said. → She told us ___ (not / be) late.
“I was sleeping,” he said. → He said he ___ (sleep).
rounds.note: Past continuous → past perfect continuous. Past continuous can stay unchanged.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: She told me she was tired.
She said to me that she was tired.
rounds.note: Tell needs a person after it; say doesn't.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He wanted to know where I lived.
rounds.answer: He asked me where did I live.
rounds.note: Reported questions use statement order, with no did.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: She asked if I was hungry.
She asked whether I was hungry.
She asked if was I hungry.
She asked me if I was hungry.
rounds.answer: She asked if was I hungry.
rounds.note: After if / whether, the subject comes before the verb.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: He told me not to leave.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: She suggested that we go out.
She suggested us to go out.
She suggested we should go out.
rounds.answer: She suggested us to go out.
rounds.note: Suggest is never followed by person + to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: He admitted to breaking the window.
He admitted to break the window.
He admitted that he had broken the window.
rounds.answer: He admitted to break the window.
rounds.note: Admit + -ing (or admit to + -ing), never to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: What pattern follows each verb?
rounds.note: Some reporting verbs take a person and to; others take -ing.

rounds.prompt: How does each direct form change?
rounds.note: Present → past simple; past simple and present perfect → past perfect.

rounds.prompt: Direct or reported time expression?
rounds.note: Time words shift when the moment of speaking has passed.

rounds.prompt: Reported or direct question?
items: She asked if I was ready.
rounds.note: Reported questions lose the question word order.

rounds.prompt: Say or tell?
rounds.note: Say hello / goodbye / sorry; tell a lie / the truth / a story.

rounds.prompt: Match each modal to its reported form.
Match each time expression to its reported form.
rounds.note: Time words move back with the tense.

rounds.prompt: Match each verb to its pattern.
rounds.note: The reporting verb decides the grammar after it.

rounds.prompt: Match each sentence to its reporting verb.
rounds.note: Reporting verbs show the speaker's purpose.

rounds.prompt: “I'm leaving tomorrow,” she said.
rounds.stem: She said she ___ the next day.
rounds.note: Present continuous → past continuous; tomorrow → the next day.

rounds.prompt: “I have never been to Rome,” he said.
“Where do you work?” she asked me.
rounds.note: Reported question: statement order, past simple.

rounds.prompt: “Do you like jazz?” he asked me.
rounds.note: Yes / no question → if + statement order.

rounds.prompt: “Don't open the door,” she told him.
“I'll lend you some money,” he said to me.
“Why don't we go to the beach?” she said.
“I didn't break the vase,” he said.

rounds.sentence: She said me that she was tired.
rounds.note: Tell + person; say has no person after it.

rounds.sentence: He asked me where did I live.
She asked me that I was ready.
rounds.note: Yes / no questions are reported with if or whether.

rounds.sentence: She said she will come the next day.
They said that they have finished.
He suggested me to see a doctor.
rounds.note: Suggest + -ing or that-clause; advise + person + to.

rounds.sentence: She apologised me for being late.
rounds.note: Apologise for + -ing, with no person after apologise.
